headline: 2 Bangladeshis among 12 killed in Houthi attack on Riyadh airport
summary: Bangladesh strongly condemns the strike on King Khalid International Airport, which left 12 dead and over 300 injured.
details: A Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, has killed 12 people and injured 309 others, according to reports.
Among the deceased are two Bangladeshi nationals. Many of the injured are reported to be in critical condition.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bangladesh has strongly condemned the attack, stating that targeting civilian infrastructure and lives is unacceptable.
The Bangladesh mission in Riyadh is currently coordinating with Saudi authorities to identify the victims and provide necessary assistance to the affected families.
The government expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia and called for an immediate end to hostilities to ensure regional peace and stability.
The attack led to significant travel disruptions, with multiple flights from Dhaka to Riyadh being cancelled following the airport's closure.
caption:
12 dead and 309 injured after a Houthi attack on Riyadh airport, including two Bangladeshi nationals.

A Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, has killed 12 people and injured 309 others, according to reports.

Among the deceased are two Bangladeshi nationals. Many of the injured are reported to be in critical condition.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bangladesh has strongly condemned the attack, stating that targeting civilian infrastructure and lives is unacceptable.

The Bangladesh mission in Riyadh is currently coordinating with Saudi authorities to identify the victims and provide necessary assistance to the affected families.

The government expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia and called for an immediate end to hostilities to ensure regional peace and stability.

The attack led to significant travel disruptions, with multiple flights from Dhaka to Riyadh being cancelled following the airport's closure.

headline_marked: Hasan Mahmud: [[First Bangladeshi pacer to claim Test hat-trick]]
headline: Hasan Mahmud: First Bangladeshi pacer to claim Test hat-trick
summary: The right-arm pacer's stunning burst in Abu Dhabi has put Bangladesh in a strong position against Afghanistan.
details: Hasan Mahmud has become the first Bangladeshi fast bowler to take a Test hat-trick, ripping through Afghanistan's lower order on the third morning of the one-off Test in Abu Dhabi.
In a dramatic burst during his 18th over, Hasan claimed three successive wickets, reducing Afghanistan to 220-8 in response to Bangladesh's first-innings total of 346.
Hasan is now only the third Bangladeshi bowler overall to achieve a Test hat-trick, joining Alok Kapali (2003) and Sohag Gazi (2013).
The hat-trick began with Ismat Alam bowled for one, followed by Qais Ahmad caught by Litton Das, and completed by trapping Zia-ur-Rehman Akbar lbw for a first-ball duck.
Afghanistan's collapse was sudden; they lost four wickets for nine runs after the start of play, reversing a stubborn partnership between Rahmat Shah and Ikram Alikhil.
Afghanistan were eventually bowled out for 240, giving Bangladesh a commanding 106-run lead heading into their second innings.
Earlier in the match, Bangladesh posted 346 in their first innings, with Tanzid Hasan scoring 83, Shadman Islam 67, and Litton Das 53.
caption:
History made in Abu Dhabi! Hasan Mahmud becomes the first-ever Bangladeshi fast bowler to take a Test hat-trick.

Hasan Mahmud has become the first Bangladeshi fast bowler to take a Test hat-trick, ripping through Afghanistan's lower order on the third morning of the one-off Test in Abu Dhabi.

In a dramatic burst during his 18th over, Hasan claimed three successive wickets, reducing Afghanistan to 220-8 in response to Bangladesh's first-innings total of 346.

Hasan is now only the third Bangladeshi bowler overall to achieve a Test hat-trick, joining Alok Kapali (2003) and Sohag Gazi (2013).

The hat-trick began with Ismat Alam bowled for one, followed by Qais Ahmad caught by Litton Das, and completed by trapping Zia-ur-Rehman Akbar lbw for a first-ball duck.

Afghanistan's collapse was sudden; they lost four wickets for nine runs after the start of play, reversing a stubborn partnership between Rahmat Shah and Ikram Alikhil.

Afghanistan were eventually bowled out for 240, giving Bangladesh a commanding 106-run lead heading into their second innings.

Earlier in the match, Bangladesh posted 346 in their first innings, with Tanzid Hasan scoring 83, Shadman Islam 67, and Litton Das 53.
